rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the first exponent the mark between i and ell is a horizontal stroke with a thick terminal, without a crossing upright; the nearby subscript i+ell has a visibly crossing plus. Thus the first exponent reads i-ell-d. In the second exponent the corresponding mark has a prominent upward/downward terminal beside the loop of ell, so a crossed plus versus a hooked minus cannot be securely separated. See crops/136_scan299_L369_first.jpg and crops/136_scan299_L369_second.jpg.
rows.note: Resolve only the first existing unsure to the written minus, retaining the author’s mathematical slip. Do not replace it with the row’s mathematically intended plus. Retain the second original \unsure{i-\ell-d|i+\ell-d}: its raised terminal makes the minus/plus reading genuinely ambiguous. The row’s assertion of two definite minuses is therefore only partly confirmed; no mathematical derivation was checked.
